hero: for the whole family, in one place.
intro: At our family medical centre in Bishkek, local and international specialists see children, teenagers, adults and expecting parents.
principles: From pregnancy and childhood to adult care.
Decisions guided by modern medical research.
Local knowledge and international expertise, together.
servicesIntro: Start with a doctor’s consultation. Your doctor helps you decide which examinations are appropriate.
services: Consultations for adults, children, teenagers and pregnant patients.
Consultations for children, including growth and development check-ups.
Gynecology consultations as part of care for the whole family.
Growth and development, vision screening, EKG, anemia and diabetes screening, and laboratory tests.
Documents and certificates for school, flights, travel, employment and insurance. Confirm availability with the clinic.
additional: Ultrasound, EKG, vision testing and audiometry.
On-site testing with our partner laboratory, Express Plus. MercyMed patients can ask about a 30% discount on lab tests.
Birth-preparation courses with the clinic’s certified doula.
languages: Consultations and reports in Kyrgyz, Russian, English, Chinese, German and French. Ask reception which clinician and language are available for your visit.
aboutIntro: MercyMed is a private outpatient medical centre in Bishkek. Our approach brings modern medical knowledge and international experience together with compassionate care.
aboutText: We care for the whole family in one place and aim to limit unnecessary investigations. Evidence-based medicine means using medical research to guide diagnosis and treatment, alongside the needs of each patient.
history: Mobile clinics in the regions of Kyrgyzstan.
The Bishkek clinic opened to continue and expand this work.
Local and international specialists care for families together.

corporate.name: For Corporate Clients
corporate.summary: Annual staff check-ups and special arrangements for students.
corporate.intro: MercyMed works with companies, schools and embassies that need a clinic for regular medical examinations in Bishkek.
topics: Discuss yearly examinations for employees. The clinic can clarify which examinations and medical documents are appropriate for your organisation.
Schools can ask about special arrangements for students and the availability of certificates for school. Confirm eligibility and terms with the clinic.
When discussing a partnership, explain who needs examinations, the approximate group size, your timetable and any report or language requirements.

education.name: Medical Education
education.summary: Training and collaboration for doctors, students and residents.
education.intro: MercyMed provides training in evidence-based practice as part of its work at the family medical centre in Bishkek.
topics: Local and international doctors share their experience. The exchange brings together evidence from medical research and knowledge of the local healthcare system.
MercyMed has previously hosted medical students for visits lasting several weeks. The team is open to discussing future opportunities for residents with training institutions.
Hospitals and medical schools can discuss training goals, learner level and timing with the clinic. Confirm availability and arrangements before making plans.
education.audience: For medical students, residents, doctors, hospitals and medical schools interested in training or collaboration.
education.inquiry: For a training inquiry, include your role, institution, what you’d like to learn and your preferred dates. Check availability and arrangements with MercyMed before making plans.

mobile-clinics.name: Mobile Clinics
mobile-clinics.summary: Outreach and charitable work in the regions of Kyrgyzstan.
mobile-clinics.intro: For more than ten years, MercyMed has provided medical consultations in the regions of Kyrgyzstan. The Bishkek clinic opened in October 2023 to continue and expand this work.
topics: The team travels to communities that invite it. A local health centre or another community host helps find a place for consultations.
The visiting team can include doctors, a nurse and support staff. They bring medicines and some laboratory tests. Visits can last one or several days, depending on local arrangements.
Community hosts can tell MercyMed where they are based, what kind of support is needed and where consultations could take place. The team can discuss what is possible.
